title: Deadlock-free transfers with tryLock
prompt:
Implement `static boolean transfer(Account from, Account to, int amount)` that can NEVER deadlock, using the tryLock-backoff pattern:
1. Acquire both account locks with `tryLock()` (use a small retry loop with backoff or a ordered attempt).
2. On success: check `from.balance() >= amount`, then move funds, release both locks, return true.
3. If either lock cannot be acquired: release whatever you hold and return false.
4. `record Account(int id, int balance)` won't do — accounts must expose `ReentrantLock lock()` and be mutable; build a small static Account class inside Solution (id, balance, lock).
5. `static boolean unsafeTransfer(...)` doing the same with plain `synchronized(from)` nested `synchronized(to)` — intentionally deadlock-prone in *structure* (tests only call it with distinct orderings to keep the suite deterministic; the lesson explains the hazard).

tests.name: successful transfer moves funds
tests.hint: Debit and credit under both locks.

tests.name: insufficient funds rejected atomically
tests.hint: Balance check under both locks; no partial moves.

tests.name: tryLock backs off a CROSS-THREAD held lock
tests.hint: Holder runs on another thread, so tryLock (R) backs off; a blocking lock() would deadlock the test.
